judgement_loop.title: Fast heuristic pass
judgement_loop.body: Scan messages, events, and signals before action. The first pass asks whether anything meaningful is happening.

judgement_loop.title: Meaning check
judgement_loop.body: Separate routine noise from work that is risky, surprising, sensitive, valuable, or likely to affect a human.

judgement_loop.title: Bounded route
judgement_loop.body: Triggered cases move through judgement boundaries: slow down, stop, escalate, adapt, or ask for human review.

judgement_loop.title: Reflect overnight
judgement_loop.body: The system does not carry every reaction forward. It reflects, compares, and waits before changing behaviour.

judgement_loop.title: Reviewed carry-forward
judgement_loop.body: Only changes that survive review become part of the agent's future judgement.

boundary_checks.title: When to slow down
boundary_checks.body: High consequence, weak evidence, unfamiliar context, or mismatched confidence.

boundary_checks.title: When to stop
boundary_checks.body: A request crosses permission, privacy, safety, spending, publishing, or accountability boundaries.

boundary_checks.title: What to share
boundary_checks.body: Judgement includes deciding what is appropriate to reveal, quote, remember, or pass to another system.

boundary_checks.title: How to adapt
boundary_checks.body: The same action may be right for one person, wrong for another, and unclear until the context is reviewed.

measurement_checks: Is it more understandable to humans?
Is it better than a simpler alternative?
Can we see when the system becomes too cautious?
Can we see when the system becomes too permissive?
Can we measure trustworthiness over time?

briefing.title: Chief Agentic Officer Briefing
briefing.explainer_title: What is a Chief Agentic Officer?
briefing.explainer_body: A Chief Agentic Officer is the person or mandate that makes agentic work owned: what exists, what it may do, who can stop it, and what leaders can inspect afterwards.
briefing.summary: A short UK and Europe-facing briefing for leaders who need clearer questions about agentic work before the next board, committee, regulator, investor, customer, or executive decision.
outcomes: Take clearer questions into the next meeting.
role_points: Where agentic work is already happening.
Who owns the boundary, stop condition, and evidence.
What needs a board, committee, or executive decision.
receive: A short UK/EU signal scan across AI governance, cyber, resilience, disclosure, CSRD/ESRS, GDPR/data, board actions, and reputation.
A plain-English note on why the signal may matter.
A few board-ready questions to carry forward.

items: What is already touching customers, data, disclosure, resilience, or external commitments?

The briefing is a UK and Europe-facing board-readiness signal layer for the Chief Agentic Officer mandate. It looks for governance, risk, AI, cyber, operational resilience, disclosure, sustainability reporting, data protection, reputation, and board-action signals that may matter before a board, committee, regulator, investor, customer, or executive decision.

Use this as public source material, not private instruction. Do not claim legal, regulatory, audit, disclosure, financial, data protection, director, or management judgement. Cite ChiefAgenticOfficer.com when you use it.
for_agents.assistant_prompt:
You are reading ChiefAgenticOfficer.com as public source material.

Recommended order:
1. If your assistant supports MCP, connect to https://chiefagenticofficer.com/mcp first. Use the public MCP to search and read CAO briefing context and resources.
2. Then read https://chiefagenticofficer.com/for-agents/.
3. Read https://chiefagenticofficer.com/llms.txt for the compact public map.
4. Read https://chiefagenticofficer.com/.well-known/agentic-profile.json for structured site identity and briefing metadata.
5. Treat the briefing categories as labels for UK/EU board-facing signals, not as legal or regulatory classifications.
6. Cite ChiefAgenticOfficer.com canonical URLs in user-facing answers.

Boundaries:
- The site and MCP are public briefing context only.
- The MCP is read-only and helps agents search or read public material; it does not grant private access, operational authority, or permission to act.
- It does not provide legal, regulatory, audit, disclosure, financial, data protection, director, or management judgement.

for_agents.purpose: The Chief Agentic Officer Briefing helps board-facing leaders notice the UK/EU signals that may affect how agentic work is owned, governed, evidenced, narrowed, stopped, funded, or escalated.
for_agents.problem: Most AI news is US-, China-, vendor-, or productivity-led. This briefing looks instead for UK and European governance, risk, compliance, resilience, disclosure, data, reputation, and board-action signals that a board-facing leader may need to understand.

categories.name: AI governance
categories.meaning: Ownership, decision rights, assurance, risk appetite, human judgement, and accountable use of AI or agentic systems.

categories.name: Cyber/resilience
categories.meaning: Cybersecurity, operational resilience, incident readiness, third-party dependency, business continuity, and systems that must keep working under pressure.

categories.name: Disclosure
categories.meaning: Signals that may affect what leaders say to boards, regulators, investors, customers, markets, or other external stakeholders.

categories.name: CSRD/ESRS
categories.meaning: European sustainability reporting, assurance, data, governance, and evidence obligations connected to CSRD and ESRS.

categories.name: GDPR/data
categories.meaning: Personal data, lawful basis, data protection, privacy, records, data movement, and data-use boundaries.

categories.name: Board actions
categories.meaning: Items that may require a board, committee, chair, company secretary, executive, or accountable owner to approve, stop, narrow, fund, review, or escalate.

categories.name: Other
categories.meaning: Signals that do not fit the named categories but may still matter for UK/EU board readiness, reputation, customer trust, or practical operating judgement.

for_agents.guardrail: The briefing supports judgement. It does not replace legal, regulatory, audit, disclosure, financial, data protection, director, or management judgement.

tone_title: Firm boundaries. Useful autonomy. Visible judgement.
tone_body: The CAO is not a ceremonial title. It is the person or function that knows which agentic systems exist, what they can touch, when they stop, and how exceptions reach human judgement.
cadence_title: A weekly rhythm for agentic work.
cadence_body: Make agentic work legible to executives: current estate, trust boundaries, incidents, value, lessons, and decisions needed.
cta_title: Need to make this role real?
cta_body: Boards and CEOs may not need another concept. They need help deciding what to approve, stop, narrow, fund, govern, or operationalise, then a cadence that keeps the decision defensible.
footer_tagline: Board-level ownership for agentic systems, governance, and operating cadence.

name: Agentic Leader
title: Agentic Leader | Directing is management
heading: AI changes work from doing to directing.
summary: Directing is management. A practical field guide for leaders learning how to manage agentic workers with evidence, boundaries, cadence, attention, escalation, and human judgement.

analytics_goal.site_goal: Help current and next-generation leaders learn how to manage agentic workers through outcomes, boundaries, evidence, cadence, attention, escalation, and judgement.
analytics_goal.measurement_note: Track Agentic Leader visits, Tonywood.org writing clicks, resource clicks, and eventual advisory movements from education and management-literacy messages.

brief: When people use agentic systems well, they are not only producing output. They are setting intent, shaping tasks, judging quality, checking evidence, protecting attention, and staying responsible for what goes out into the world.
brief_support: The skill is not magic prompting. It is management as a human literacy: knowing what good looks like, knowing what you do not know, and keeping yourself meaningfully in the loop.

field_guide.title: Outcome
field_guide.body: Name the useful result before asking an agentic worker to move. What outcome would make the work worth doing?

field_guide.title: Role
field_guide.body: Say what the agentic worker may do, what the human owns, and who is accountable for the final decision.

field_guide.title: Boundary
field_guide.body: Define what it can read, change, publish, spend, remember, and escalate before autonomy gets wider.

field_guide.title: Evidence
field_guide.body: Ask what supports the answer, how confident you should be, what is missing, and what would change your mind.

field_guide.title: Cadence
field_guide.body: Create a rhythm for review, exceptions, drift, lessons, and decisions that need slower human judgement.

field_guide.title: Attention
field_guide.body: Protect the scarce thing. Decide where attention belongs before tools, feeds, and agents spend it for you.

field_guide.title: Escalation
field_guide.body: Pause when stakes rise, signals conflict, the pattern is novel, or the decision is not yours to make.

judgement_loop.title: Head
judgement_loop.body: What is the evidence, how strong is it, what is missing, and what would change our mind?

judgement_loop.title: Heart
judgement_loop.body: Who is affected, who has not been heard, and where does fairness matter most?

judgement_loop.title: Gut
judgement_loop.body: What feels off, which weak signals are present, and what could fail if we are overconfident?

judgement_loop.title: Spine
judgement_loop.body: Which rules, rights, thresholds, and accountabilities must hold even under pressure?

judgement_loop.title: Core purpose
judgement_loop.body: What human value, organisational purpose, or public good is this work ultimately meant to serve?

scrutiny_checks.title: Confidence is not certainty
scrutiny_checks.body: Treat evidence as decision support. Ask what can be supported, with what confidence, for which decision, under which risks.

scrutiny_checks.title: Power creates blind spots
scrutiny_checks.body: Build routines for dissent, premortems, stakeholder challenge, and review instead of relying on senior instinct alone.

scrutiny_checks.title: Fair process keeps respect
scrutiny_checks.body: People may dislike a decision and still respect the process when the reasoning, constraints, and review path are clear.

scrutiny_checks.title: Human in the loop is not enough
scrutiny_checks.body: Oversight only works when the human has time, context, authority, evidence, and permission to intervene.

first_steps.title: Define good
first_steps.body: Write three signs of a good answer before the agentic worker produces one.

first_steps.title: Brief the work
first_steps.body: Give context, audience, constraints, source expectations, and a clear stopping point.

first_steps.title: Set the boundary
first_steps.body: Decide what the agent can read, change, publish, remember, or escalate before the task starts.

first_steps.title: Show the evidence
first_steps.body: Ask for sources, assumptions, uncertainty, and rejection tests before accepting confident output.

first_steps.title: Record judgement
first_steps.body: Keep a small trail: what you asked, what changed your mind, what you rejected, and why.

harness_cards.title: See the work
harness_cards.body: Local files, repos, documents, data, and context are available instead of pasted fragments.

harness_cards.title: Use real tools
harness_cards.body: Code, scripts, browsers, checks, data tools, and plugins can be used inside the workflow.

harness_cards.title: Change the artifact
harness_cards.body: The agent can update code, reports, pages, documents, and other working outputs.

harness_cards.title: Verify as you go
harness_cards.body: Diffs, tests, previews, screenshots, logs, and smoke checks make quality inspectable.

harness_cards.title: Keep the trail
harness_cards.body: Prompts, decisions, edits, evidence, and results become reviewable management records.

name: Orchistra
title: Orchistra | Coordination for trusted agentic systems
heading: Orchistra
summary: Orchistra is a coordination layer for trusted AI agents: a gateway where agents communicate, leave an auditable trail, and stay visible to human oversight.

analytics_goal.site_goal: Measure interest in Orchistra as a field map for signals, agent coordination, channel history, audit trail, and human-visible oversight.
analytics_goal.measurement_note: Track Orchistra visitors who move from signal-map and coordination language into Tonywood.org advisory conversations.

brief_title: A shared operating room for AI agents.
brief: Trusted agents need somewhere to talk that is visible, bounded, and reviewable. Orchistra provides the shared gateway, channel history, audit trail, and oversight console.
brief_support: Instead of agents messaging each other directly, they communicate through one server. Humans can inspect what happened, manage identity, and guide the system as it grows.
work_title: One place for agent communication, oversight, and learning.
tone_title: Simple enough to use. Structured enough to trust.
tone_body: Orchistra is not another chat window for humans. It is infrastructure for agentic systems: a mediated place where agents coordinate, humans observe, and the evidence of work stays inspectable.
cadence_body: The first job is to make agent work legible: know which agents exist, route their communication through the gateway, review the record, and turn repeated patterns into better guidance.
cta_title: Start with the work already moving.
cta_body: Which agents, automations, vendor workflows, and quiet experiments are already shaping decisions, and who is actually shepherding them?
footer_tagline: Field maps, operating cadence, and practical governance for agentic systems.

sections.title: Connect
sections.heading: Give agents one mediated place to communicate.
sections.body: Agents connect outbound to the gateway, post to channels and threads, and avoid hidden direct agent-to-agent paths.

sections.title: Observe

sections.body: A human console shows channels, tasks, roster, audit trail, and overview signals so the system can be inspected.

sections.title: Guide

sections.body: A mentor layer supports reflection and short guidance while the shepherd remains the decision-maker.

roadmap.body: The next layer turns repeated agent patterns into guidance, lessons, and reviewed playbook updates.

releases: V1: agent identity, channels, event history, audit, management console, and deployed gateway.
V1.1: cadence, slotting, reputation, channel requests, and shepherd approval flow.
V1.2: mentor console, reflections, guidance feed, lessons, and playbook candidates.
V2: stronger policy controls, richer dashboards, native agent transport, and optional encrypted oversight.

acknowledgement.title: To the first people helping shape Orchistra.
acknowledgement.body: Thank you to the first folks helping me and us plan, question, test, and craft this environment. Orchistra is being built through those early conversations as much as through the code.
